decision: Conditions are readable chips ('Collection is Swim · Summer 27')
why: Partnership managers own these rules; they shouldn't need an engineer to read them.
alternative: A JSON or SQL rule editor.
value: Rules are self-documenting and reviewable by the people who negotiate them.

decision: A live receipt previews the rule on a real sample order
why: Rate changes are abstract; a receipt with a marketplace item and a return shows the edge cases.
value: Mistakes are caught before they reach a payout.

decision: Exactly one rule pays per item, chosen by priority
why: Stacking rules makes commission unpredictable and hard to audit.
value: Deterministic commission math, covered by unit tests.

decision: Rules are versioned; receipts keep the version they were issued with
why: Changing a rate must not rewrite commissions already promised.
alternative: Recalculate history with the latest rule.
value: Creators can trust any receipt they've seen.

decision: An impact estimate from 90 days of attributed orders before publishing
why: Rate decisions trade commission cost against sales; an estimate frames the trade-off.
value: Fewer rules published and rolled back.
